title: Implementation Mosaic - Customer milestone tracker (template)
content:
Context:
This is a lightweight, column-first tracker intended for Customer Success managers running inference rollouts (hosted/dedicated/private). It balances granularity with ease-of-update for weekly QBR syncs and fast escalations. Use this as the canonical short-form status doc for a single customer engagement.

How to use:
- Keep one row per milestone/sub-project (eg. infra, model-onboarding, privacy & networking, acceptance tests).
- Update RAG and percent complete before weekly partner sync.
- Add short "last update" note and link to primary artifact (PR, runbook, ticket).
- Use Milestone ID when referencing in Slack/Jira for quick lookups.

Definitions (brief):
- Owner: CS or Solutions Eng single point of contact.
- Dependent On: external teams or customer items that must complete first.
- Customer Impact: what breaks or improves when this milestone completes.
- Blocker Summary: one-line blocker + "who" and ETA for unblock.
- Severity: High/Med/Low relative to go-live SLA.

Columns (copy into sheet or keep as sectioned doc):
1) Milestone ID | 2) Title | 3) Owner | 4) Target date | 5) % complete | 6) RAG | 7) Acceptance criteria (1-2 lines) | 8) Dependent on | 9) Customer impact | 10) Active blocker (if any) | 11) Blocker owner / ETA | 12) Last update (date + 1-line) | 13) Primary artifact link

Example rows (sample entries to copy):
- M-01 | Network peering + firewall rules | Priya Nair | 2026-03-04 | 85% | Amber | VPC peering established, egress rules validated by infra | Customer infra team: provide CIDR blocks; Redwood infra to configure peering | Customer app can call hosted endpoints with <100ms added latency | Blocker: customer security requires additional SOW for peering review | Blocker owner: Customer Sec (K. Tanaka) / ETA: 2026-03-10 | Last update: 2026-02-20 — awaiting signed SOW | https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/networking-peering-M-01

- M-07 | Model validation & acceptance tests | Ethan Zhang | 2026-03-12 | 40% | Red | 5 canonical prompts pass accuracy threshold + perf within latency SLO | Dependent on labeled eval set from customer & test harness | Failure to pass blocks go-live and could require model variant | Blocker: missing labeled eval set (customer delayed) | Blocker owner: Customer PM (S. Lopez) / ETA: 2026-03-15 | Last update: 2026-02-23 — RBC sent reminder | JIRA-4827

- M-11 | KV-cache tuning and perf run | Lena Orlov | 2026-03-01 | 100% | Green | KV cache achieves 2.6x token throughput without increased tail latency | Dependent on runtime image rollout (done) | Improves cost per token by ~38% | Blocker: none | Blocker owner / ETA: n/a | Last update: 2026-02-28 — perf report uploaded | https://github.com/redwood-inference/ops/issues/912

Escalation matrix (short):
- Tier 1 (CS owner): first contact — Morgan Reyes — slack #cs-redwood — phone on-call
- Tier 2 (Solutions Eng): Ethan Zhang — escalate if blocker >48h or severity High
- Tier 3 (Infra/Runtime): On-call infra lead (page via PagerDuty) — for production perf issues

Risk scoring (quick heuristic to prioritize):
- Score 1-5 where 5 = highest risk to go-live. Factors: blocker severity, dependency complexity, customer SLA impact, regulatory gating.
- Add score in notes when RAG=Red.

Weekly QBR agenda snippet (2 pages max):
- 5m: quick health (RAG snapshot across milestones)
- 10m: discuss top 2 blockers and owners/next steps
- 10m: decisions required this week (SOW approvals, infra windows)
- 5m: action items & owners (add to tracker, due dates)

Playbook snippets (copyable actions):
- If model acceptance is blocked >72h due to missing eval data, escalate to customer PM + CS director and propose interim synthetic eval set for perf gating.
- If network peering delayed beyond the agreed window, offer temporary TLS tunnel with IP allowlist and document increased latency/cost risk.
- If performance regression observed after runtime change, rollback to previous runtime image and open postmortem; label regression in Redwood Optimize as a quality alert.

Notes to self / Work-in-progress items (informal):
- Consider adding "estimated cost impact" column for dedicated customers to quantify cost delta per milestone (helpful in renewal conversations).
- Want to prototype a short form that feeds direct into QBR slides (auto-generate RAG smallcards).
- Follow up with Product (hosting) on adding a single-click link to runtime traces from the tracker.

Open questions for next CS sync:
- Should we standardize acceptance threshold templates per use case (summarization, chat, embeddings)?
- Do we prefer percent complete be owner-estimated or a derived metric from checklist items?

Quick checklist for when a milestone turns Green: (owner confirms)
- Acceptance criteria documented and signed-off by customer
- Primary artifact linked and accessible to CS/SE teams
- Any post-go-live mitigations (observability hooks, alerts) created in Console
- Update billing/renewal queue if milestone affects committed capacity

Footer (links & history):
- Template created by Morgan Reyes 2025-11-05. Iteration log: converted to "mosaic" approach 2026-01-14; added risk heuristic 2026-02-18; QBR agenda condensed 2026-02-25.
- Slack references: #cs-redwood, #cs-esc-ops.

---
This file is intentionally concise and meant for fast updates; copy rows into a sheet for filter/sort or sync to the customer-facing tracker if needed.
